title: Krishna Uproots the Parijata Tree in Nandana
one_line_summary: Under pretext of hunting, Krishna rides Garuda to Indra's Nandana garden, uproots the heavenly Parijata tree before the celestial guards, and carries it off on Garuda's back.
source_excerpt: the illustrious Adhokshaja saw hosts of celestial warriors... That refuge of the pious, the mighty Krishna uprooted the Pārijāta tree and placed it on the back of Garuda even before their eyes

title: Indra Challenges Krishna over the Parijata
one_line_summary: The garden-keepers alert Indra, who rides out on Airavata and demands Krishna return the Parijata, challenging him to battle for it.
source_excerpt: Sakra replied saying,—"O lotus-eyed one, thou shouldst not take away this tree, O infallible one, without challenging me to fight"

title: Pradyumna Duels Jayanta in the Sky
one_line_summary: Pradyumna, son of Rukmini, battles Indra's son Jayanta; a heavenly weapon burns Pradyumna's chariot to ashes yet cannot harm him, who stands firm in the sky.
source_excerpt: a fierce combat raged between the heroic Jayanta and the son of Rukshmini... The car of the illustrious Pradyumna was burnt down by that weapon but it could not... consume the son of Rukshmini

title: Satyaki Fights the Brahmana Pravara; Garuda Strikes Him Down
one_line_summary: Satyaki duels the twice-born warrior Pravara, who repeatedly disarms him; when Pravara tries to seize the Parijata, Garuda's wing-blow hurls him and his car four miles back.
source_excerpt: Garuda struck him with his wings so vehemently that he, with his car, fell full four miles back and there fainted away
notes: Pravara is a Brahmana disciple of Jamadagni's son Rama, invincible by a boon from Brahma; Satyaki refuses to slay a Brahmana.

title: Garuda Fells Airavata from Heaven
one_line_summary: Garuda fights Indra's elephant Airavata, striking it with claws and talons until the wounded elephant falls from the heights of heaven onto the Parijatra mountain.
source_excerpt: Garuda, of mighty strength, struck Airāvata on the head with his fierce claws furnished with fearful talons. Afflicted sorely with the wound... the elephant fell from the heights of heaven on the top of that best of mountains the Pārijātra

title: Krishna Worships Shiva and Wins His Boon
one_line_summary: Pausing the fight at nightfall, Krishna performs ablutions in the Ganga, eulogizes Shiva with a hymn, and Shiva appears with Uma, granting that he shall carry away the Parijata and remain invincible.
source_excerpt: Thus eulogised the god Mahādeva... spoke to Nārāyana:—"O best of gods, thou shalt obtain the things desired by thee; thou shalt carry away the Pārijāta tree... thou shalt be invincible"
notes: Devotional interlude during the Parijata campaign; establishes Krishna's Shiva-hymn (Rudra-stuti).

title: Shiva Reveals the Danava Stronghold of Satpura
one_line_summary: Shiva tells Krishna of the Danavas hidden in the Satpura stronghold beneath the mountain — invincible to the gods by Brahma's boon — and Krishna is enshrined on the Parijatra mountain.
source_excerpt: on the summit of this mountain... there is a stronghold of the Dānavas called Satpura. Hidden inside that fastness live mighty Dānavas of wicked soul... do thou, O Keshava, slay them
notes: Sets up the Satpura campaign of chs. 230-232; Krishna also grants the mountain the name Sanapada and is enshrined there.

title: Kashyapa and Aditi Reconcile Krishna and Indra
one_line_summary: Sent by Brahma, the parents Kashyapa and Aditi halt the battle, and the two 'brothers' lay down their arms, bathe in the Jahnvi, and are reconciled.
source_excerpt: holding them both by the hands Aditi said:—"Born of the same parents you are trying to slay each other as if you are not brothers... lay down your arms and hear what I say"

title: Aditi Grants the Parijata; Krishna Brings It to Satyabhama
one_line_summary: Aditi grants Krishna the Parijata for Satyabhama's rite on condition of its return; Krishna plants it at Raivataka and carries it into Dwarka, where Satyabhama receives it joyfully.
source_excerpt: Aditi... said to Hari:—"O Upendra! take this Pārijāta, go to Dwarkā and perform the auspicious festival so longed for by your wife... you are to bring back this tree"... taking that best of trees Pārijāta he entered into Satyabhāmā's palace
notes: The Parijata is granted on the condition it be returned to Nandana after the rite (fulfilled ch. 223).

title: Satyabhama's Punyaka Rite and the Gift to Narada
one_line_summary: Satyabhama binds Krishna to the Parijata, dedicates him to the sage Narada, and gifts gold, kine and jewels; Narada releases him for a fee, and Satyabhama distributes celestial garments to the sixteen thousand wives.
source_excerpt: the lucky damsel, having put a garland of flowers around Krishna's neck, bound him to the Pārijāta tree... she dedicated Keshava unto Nārada... she gave away... mountains of gold and a thousand kine

title: Krishna Returns the Parijata and Vows to Destroy the Danavas
one_line_summary: After a year of festival, Krishna returns the Parijata to heaven, and before Indra vows to slay, within ten days, the Danavas that the gods cannot kill.
source_excerpt: From to-day within ten days I will kill all those Asuras... Although those Dānavas, proud of the boon conferred on them by Brahmā, are unslayable by the gods, still we will kill them for I am now a man
notes: Bridges directly into the Satpura war of chs. 230-232.

title: The Danavas Demand a Share of Brahmadatta's Yajna
one_line_summary: At the Brahmana Brahmadatta's year-long sacrifice in Shatpura, the Danava Nikumbha and his kin demand Soma, jewels and the Brahmana's daughters, threatening to disrupt the rite.
source_excerpt: Nikumbha and other Daityas, proud of their boon, assembled there and said:—"Give us our share in the Yajna. We will drink Soma and Brahmadatta must give us his daughters"
notes: Brahmadatta is the friend and preceptor of Krishna's father Vasudeva, who attends to protect him.

title: Pradyumna Saves the Maidens by Illusion
one_line_summary: When the Danavas scatter the sacrifice and carry off Brahmadatta's daughters, Pradyumna, sent by Krishna, rescues the maidens by illusion, leaving only counterfeit figures for the demons.
source_excerpt: Pradyumna... went to Shatpura within a moment and took away the maidens by virtue of his illusive power. Creating their figures by his illusive power... he kept them before the Daityas

title: Narada Incites the Kings to Aid the Asuras
one_line_summary: Narada, foreseeing a clash at the crowded sacrifice, prompts the Asuras to bribe the assembled kings with jewels and maidens so they will fight the Yadavas — while warning the Pandavas to hold back.
source_excerpt: Nārada... said to Nikumbha:—"...O hero, you invite in proper order the help of other kings..." ...returning... the great Nārada prevented the heroic sons of Pandu

title: Nikumbha Imprisons the Yadava Heroes by Maya
one_line_summary: Using his illusive powers, Nikumbha carries Anadhrishti, Kritavarma, Charudeshna and many other Yadavas one by one into the Shatpura cave and imprisons them, enraging Krishna and Baladeva.
source_excerpt: by his illusive powers, took there Kritavarmā, Chārudeshna, Vaitarana... and numerous other Yādavas... he led the Yadavas to the dreadful cave of Shatpura

title: Krishna Routs the Asuras with the Sarnga Bow
one_line_summary: Krishna, with his Sarnga bow, consumes the Danava host like fire on grass, while Jayanta and Pravara slay from the sky every Asura who tries to escape upward.
source_excerpt: setting string to his Srānga bow... Krishna began to move about amongst the Dānavas as the god of fire ranges on grass... as soon as they rose up into the sky Jayanta and Pravara killed them all with arrows

title: Pradyumna Binds the Bribed Kings with Shiva's Nooses
one_line_summary: Bearing nooses given by Hara and commanded by Nandi, Pradyumna binds Sisupala, Bhagadatta, Rukmi and the other kings who sided with the Asuras, and holds them in the illusory cave.
source_excerpt: binding the king Bhagadatta, Shishupāla, Ahvati, Rukshmi and other kings... with the nooses given by Hara Rukshmini's son... took them all to the illusory cave

title: Krishna Slays Nikumbha with the Sudarshana Discus
one_line_summary: As the routed Asuras return to fight, Krishna follows Nikumbha into the Shatpura cave and, commanded by an invisible voice to use his discus, cuts off the demon's head with the Sudarshana.
source_excerpt: saluting Mahādeva he discharged his discus Sudarshana... That discus, effulgent like the solar disc... sundered Nikumbha's head adorned with most beautiful ear-rings
notes: Nikumbha had three bodies by Shiva's boon, invincible to all but Hara; Krishna had earlier destroyed one body while carrying away Bhanumati.

title: Krishna Distributes the Spoils and Grants Shatpura to Brahmadatta
one_line_summary: After the victory, Krishna gives the Daitya maidens to the Yadavas, jewels and raiment to the kings, six thousand chariots to the Pandavas, and the city of Shatpura to Brahmadatta.
source_excerpt: Keshava... conferred upon the Yadavas hundreds of Daitya maidens... he gave the Pāndavas six thousand cars with horses... gave that city of Shatpura to the Brāhmana Brahmadatta

title: Krishna Sports with His Sixteen Thousand Wives in the Ocean
one_line_summary: Sailing to the shrine of Pindaraka, the Yadavas sport in the ocean; Krishna sports simultaneously with his sixteen thousand wives, each believing she alone is his favourite, while he makes the salt ocean sweet.
source_excerpt: amongst the women of Keshava every one thought:—"I am the most favourite of Keshava: he is sporting only with me"... at the command of Vāsudeva the water of the ocean was freed from salt
notes: Descriptive sport chapter; Krishna's simultaneous presence with each wife is a celebrated devotional theme.

title: Krishna Brings the Celestial Chhalikya Song to the Yadavas
one_line_summary: Krishna stages a music soiree: Narada plays the vina, Krishna dances the Hallishaka with his flute, and the Apsaras Rambha and Urvashi perform, as the celestial Chhalikya song is brought down for mankind.
source_excerpt: Narada began to play on his Vinā... Krishna began to perform Hallishaka accompanied with the music of his flute... the beautiful Rambhā... rose up, played and pleased Rāma and Keshava
notes: Largely a glory/music interlude; the chapter also recaps prior exploits (Kaliya, Govardhana, etc.) already indexed elsewhere.

title: Nikumbha Carries Away Bhanumati
one_line_summary: While the Yadavas are absorbed in ocean sport, the Danava Nikumbha, avenging Pradyumna's earlier abduction of Prabhavati, steals Bhānu's daughter Bhanumati from her unguarded garden.
source_excerpt: the highly wicked and unapproachable Dānava, Nikumbha... stole away the beautiful daughter of Bhānu by name Bhānumati... Taking advantage of this weak moment the wretched Dānava carried away the maiden
notes: Nikumbha acts in revenge for Pradyumna's earlier taking of Prabhavati and slaying of Vajranabha.

title: Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna Pursue the Abductor
one_line_summary: Krishna, Arjuna and Pradyumna overtake Nikumbha on Garuda; careful not to wound the maiden, they pierce him with cane-like arrows as he flees across the earth, and Pradyumna recovers Bhanumati.
source_excerpt: Pārtha, Krishna and Kāma... did not strike the maiden but wounded the Danavas with their cane-like arrows... Pradyumna... got hold of the maiden Bhānumati. And Krishna, and Arjuna began to assail the Asura greatly with arrows

title: Nikumbha Fells Arjuna and Pradyumna; Krishna Duels Him
one_line_summary: Emerging from the Shatpura cave, Nikumbha knocks Arjuna and Pradyumna senseless with his thorned club; enraged, Krishna seizes Kaumodaki and fights him in single combat.
source_excerpt: Nikumbha... struck Pārtha on his head... Wounded on the head with that unseen stroke of the club the heroic Pradyumna lost his consciousness... Govinda... took up his club Koumodaki and ran towards Nikumbha

title: Krishna Destroys a Body of Nikumbha with the Discus
one_line_summary: As Nikumbha's illusion fills earth and sky with a thousand of his forms, Krishna, perceiving the true form with celestial wisdom, cuts off its head with his discus and frees the abducted Arjuna.
source_excerpt: they saw all over the earth and welkin thousands of Nikumbha... the Divine Lord Krishna... saw the true form of Nikumbha, the creator of illusions... with his discus, cut off his head
notes: Nikumbha has three bodies by Shiva's boon; the episode order across chs. 232 and 237 is non-linear in the text.

title: Narada Reveals Bhanumati's Fate; She Weds Sahadeva
one_line_summary: Narada explains that Bhanumati's abduction was the working of a Durvasa curse softened by the sages; Bhānu then gives her in marriage to Sahadeva.
source_excerpt: on one occasion... this your daughter excited the anger of the foremost of Munis Durvāsā who... imprecated a curse on her saying:—'...she must fall into the hands of an enemy'... do you now confer her on Sahadeva

title: Vajranabha Wins His Boon and Demands the Three Worlds
one_line_summary: By austerities on Sumeru, the Asura Vajranabha wins from Brahma the unconquerable city Vajra and immunity from the gods, then challenges Indra for the sovereignty of the three worlds.
source_excerpt: Vajranābha... prayed for two boons that even the gods might not kill him, and that he might get the city Vajra... he said "O slayer of Pāka, all the three worlds are the common properties... I therefore wish to govern the three worlds... give me battle"

title: Krishna's Stratagem: the Actor Bhadra and the Swan Emissaries
one_line_summary: Indra consults Krishna, who promises to slay Vajranabha after Vasudeva's horse-sacrifice; an actor named Bhadra wins a boon of entering the impenetrable city, and Indra sends swans to win Prabhavati for Pradyumna.
source_excerpt: Indra... said to Dhārtarāshtra swans:—"...Do you describe to her the various accomplishments... of the high-souled Pradyumna... An actor, Bhadra by name, has of late obtained the boon (of entering into his city)"
notes: Setup for the Vajranabha destruction, which continues in chapters outside this bundle.

title: The Yadavas Enter Vajra Disguised as Actors
one_line_summary: Disguised as actors, the Yadavas enter Vajranabha's impenetrable city and perform the Ramayana and Rambhabhisara so skilfully that the Danavas shower them with jewels until their own wealth is drained.
source_excerpt: the Daityas, living in branch cities, took the Yadavas, disguised as actors, to the charming city of Vajra... Giving away presents in this way at every scene those Dānavas were deprived of their riches and jewels
notes: The troupe performs the Ramayana and the drama Rambhabhisara; Pradyumna plays Nalakuvara, Shura plays Ravana.

title: Pradyumna in Bee Form Meets Prabhavati
one_line_summary: Pradyumna, aided by Prabhavati's goose friend Suchimukhi, assumes the form of a bee hidden in a flower-garland, alights on Prabhavati's ear, and the long-pining lovers meet by night.
source_excerpt: seeing a fragrant garland filled with bees carried for Prabhāvati, the highly powerful... Pradyumna... sat there on assuming the form of a bee... the heroic Bhaima chief slowly sat on Prabhāvati's ear

title: Kashyapa Warns Vajranabha, Who Marches on Heaven
one_line_summary: After Kashyapa's sacrifice, Vajranabha rejects his father's warning that he cannot vanquish Indra and sets out with his kinsmen to conquer the celestial region.
source_excerpt: you will not be able to vanquish him but yourself will be killed... Vajrānābha did not approve of the words of Kashyapa... He first set out for conquering the region of the celestials
notes: The three princesses have already borne youthful, omniscient sons (Chandraprabha, Gunavan) who are raised in Indra's palaces.

title: The Danava Princesses Arm Their Yadava Husbands
one_line_summary: When Vajranabha orders the arrest of the young Yadava sons, Prabhavati hands Pradyumna a sword and blesses him with victory, while Chandravati and Gunavati arm Gada and Shamba.
source_excerpt: Prabhāvati... handed over a sword to Rukshmini's son... saying, "Acquire victory"... Chandravati delightfully gave to Gada one Nishtringsha and Gunavati gave another such weapon to the highly powerful Shāmva

title: Pradyumna Fights with Ananta as Charioteer
one_line_summary: Pradyumna creates a celestial car with the thousand-headed serpent Ananta as charioteer and devastates the Asura host, while Indra sends his own car, Airavata and Jayanta to aid the Yadavas.
source_excerpt: Pradyumna... created a car with his Māyā. He made the thousand-headed Nāga Ananta... his charioteer... he began to move about in the midst of the Asura army... three fourths of the Asuras were killed

title: Pradyumna Duels Vajranabha
one_line_summary: Riding Garuda, Pradyumna wounds Vajranabha, who in turn fells him with a club; the sound of Krishna's Panchajanya conch revives the fallen hero.
source_excerpt: The highly powerful Vrajranābha was wounded on the breast with a club by the high-souled Krishna's son... Pradyumna, vomitted blood and lost his conciousness... At the sound of that Panchanjanya... Pradyumna revived and stood up

title: Pradyumna Slays Vajranabha with Krishna's Discus
one_line_summary: Krishna's discus comes into Pradyumna's hand, and with it he severs Vajranabha's head, while Gada slays Sunabha and Shamba destroys the remaining Asuras.
source_excerpt: his discus... came into the hand of his son... that discus, discharged by Nārāyana's son, separated Vajranābha's head from his body... The dreadful Sunābha... was killed by Gada

title: Indra and Krishna Install the Four Young Kings
one_line_summary: Indra and Krishna divide Vajranabha's conquered kingdom into four parts and anoint the four young princes — Vijaya and the sons of Pradyumna, Shamba and Gada — as kings of the Vajra realm.
source_excerpt: Indra and Upendra divided Vajranābha's kingdom into four parts... one-fourth... to Jayanta's son Vijaya, one-fourth to Pradyumna's son, one-fourth to Shāmva's son and the remaining one-fourth to Gada's son Chandraprabha
notes: The sons were anointed with Ganga water; Pradyumna, Gada and Shamba returned to Dwarka after six months.

title: Vishwakarma Adorns Dwarka for Krishna
one_line_summary: At Indra's request, the celestial architect Vishwakarma beautifies Dwarka after Amaravati, building golden palaces for each of Krishna's queens, and Krishna enters the adorned city.
source_excerpt: the king of gods sent for the celestial Architect and said:—"...do you... make his beautiful city more exquisite..." Vishwakarmā adorned it after Amarāvati... he built a highly beautiful golden palace... for Rukshmini
notes: Embellishment (not the founding) of Dwarka; largely a descriptive glorification chapter with a thin narrative frame.

title: Krishna Returns to Dwarka and Honors Naraka's Captive Maidens
one_line_summary: Krishna re-enters Dwarka with the Parijata and the treasure-mountain, blows the Panchajanya to the citizens' joy, and honors the maidens freed from Naraka's house with garments, riches and homes.
source_excerpt: he blew his conch the sound of which made the hairs of his enemies stand erect... honored all the maidens he had brought from Naraka's house with raiments, ornaments, maid-servants, riches... Krishna allotted to each of those women, separate houses, tanks, and gardens

title: The Yogamaya Appears Before Krishna and Rama
one_line_summary: The illusory daughter of Yashoda — the goddess born the same moment as Krishna — appears before Krishna and Rama, who embrace her and seat her between them as the Vrishni women worship her.
source_excerpt: the illusory daughter of Yashoda... appeared before Krishna and Rāma... Mādhava approached her... and held her by the hand. The highly powerful Rāma too... embraced her and smelt her head... The Vrishni women then saw her between her two brothers Rāma and Krishna
notes: The goddess Yogamaya was substituted for Krishna at birth and would have been killed by Kamsa; here she is revealed to the Yadavas.

title: Narada Prophesies the Ocean Will Swallow Dwarka
one_line_summary: Before departing, Narada prophesies that Krishna, having fulfilled the gods' work, will let the ocean inundate Dwarka and Bhogavati, and will be united with Narayana.
source_excerpt: the highly illustrious Krishna will make the ocean devour the cities Bhogavati... and Dwārakā... The ocean, conversant with the desire of Krishna... will inundate this city of Dwārakā
notes: Foreshadows the end of the Yadavas and Krishna's departure; the rest of chs. 248-249 is a recap of prior exploits already indexed elsewhere.

title: Shamvara Steals the Infant Pradyumna
one_line_summary: On the seventh night after his birth, the Danava Kalashamvara steals the infant Pradyumna from Rukmini's lying-in room and carries him to his city, where his wife Mayavati receives the child.
source_excerpt: On the seventh day at dead of night Kalashamvara stole away that infant son of Krishna from the lying-in room... His beautiful and accomplished wife Māyāvati... gave over that son of Vasudeva to her like his own
notes: Pradyumna is Kama (Cupid) reborn; Krishna, knowing all by his maya, holds back so Pradyumna may be Shamvara's destined slayer.

title: Mayavati Reveals the Truth to Pradyumna
one_line_summary: When the grown Pradyumna recoils at Mayavati's advances, she reveals he is not her son but the child of Rukmini and Vasudeva, stolen by Shamvara, and that she is his former wife.
source_excerpt: You are not my son, nor Shamvara is your father... you are the delightful son of Vāsudeva and Rukshmini... you were stolen by my powerful husband... I seek you as my lover, because I have not given birth to you

title: Pradyumna Fells Shamvara's Standard to Provoke Him
one_line_summary: To draw out the Danava who stole him, Pradyumna strikes down Shamvara's lion-emblazoned standard, and the enraged Shamvara sends his hundred sons to kill him.
source_excerpt: I will strike down the wonderful standard... having the emblem of a lion which stands like the mount Sumeru on his gate... Hearing of the spoliation of his standard... Shamvara, filled with anger, ordered his sons... "do you soon kill Rukshmini's son"

title: Pradyumna Slays the Hundred Sons of Shamvara
one_line_summary: In a single battle, Pradyumna cuts down all hundred of Shamvara's sons who come against him, and stands victorious awaiting the father.
source_excerpt: he killed the ten highly powerful sons of Shamvara... Having thus slain one hundred sons of Shamvara, all good bow men, he stood in the battle field desirous of fighting

title: Pradyumna Slays Shamvara's Four Ministers
one_line_summary: Pradyumna slays the four Danava ministers — Durdhara, Ketumali, Shatruhanta and Pramardana — one by one, and their army flees in terror.
source_excerpt: he shot it at the breast of the short-lived Durdhara... with it before all he cut off Ketumāli's head... the heart of the highly powerful Shatruhantā was cut off... Kāma... crushed down Pramarddana with that club

title: Shamvara's Illusions and Pradyumna's Counters
one_line_summary: Shamvara hurls illusory trees, stones, lions and a serpent-maya at Pradyumna, who counters each with fiery weapons and a Garuda illusion, to the applause of the gods.
source_excerpt: Shamvara... created a great illusory display by throwing on Pradyumna's car lions, tigers, bears, monkeys... Kāma however, with Gandharva weapons, cut them off into many pieces... Garudas began to move about and destroy the venomous serpents

title: Narada Reveals Pradyumna's True Identity and Arms Him
one_line_summary: Sent by Indra, Narada reminds Pradyumna of his former birth as Kama, gives him the Vaishnava weapons and a coat of mail, and bids him slay Shamvara and reclaim his wife Mayavati.
source_excerpt: Nārada... said to Pradyumna:—"...remember your pristine birth. O hero, you are Kāma... having killed Shamvara in the battle-field with Vaishnava weapons take your own wife Māyāvati and go to Dwārakā"

title: Pradyumna Returns to Dwarka and Is Recognized
one_line_summary: Pradyumna descends from the sky with Mayavati into Krishna's apartments; Rukmini, moved by a dream and by the marks of the Vrishni race, recognizes her lost son, and Krishna reveals that Mayavati is Rati, Kama's wife.
source_excerpt: Pradyumna... rose up into the welkin and reached the charming city of Dwāravati... Rukshmini... said:—"Blessed is that woman whose son is such a beautiful... boy resembling Kāma"... Krishna... said:—"...here is your son the great bow-man. He has killed Shamvara... Know her as Rati, the beloved consort of Kāma"

title: Narada's Riddle: Who Is Truly Great
one_line_summary: When Narada cryptically hails Krishna as 'wonder and blessed' and Krishna answers 'presents', the puzzled kings ask the meaning; Narada recounts a journey from tortoise to Ganga, ocean, earth, mountains, Brahma, the Vedas and the Yajnas, each deferring to the next, until the riddle resolves in Vishnu with dakshina.
source_excerpt: Nārada... said... "O thou of large arms, thou alone hast become an object of wonder to the gods"... Krishna, smilingly said:—"Yes I am an object of surprise and good luck, especially in the matter of presents"... Vishnu alone is the great wonder... great is a Yajna accompanied with presents
notes: Didactic parable on the chain of greatness; framed by a royal assembly at Dwarka.

title: Krishna Crosses the Ocean and the Cosmic Mountains
one_line_summary: Seeking to recover a Brahmana's lost sons, Krishna and Arjuna cross the ocean, whose waters part to admit his car, and pass the seven cosmic mountains, which bow and grant passage.
source_excerpt: the ocean again said to Janārddana:—"...I will dry up the path in which your car... will proceed"... we proceeded through that lustrous red water as if we were on land... the mountains... said:—"What are we to do?"... "You are to give me passage"
notes: Told by Arjuna in retrospect; the ocean and mountains personified submit to Krishna.

title: Krishna Recovers the Brahmana's Four Sons
one_line_summary: Krishna enters the vast effulgence beyond the darkness and returns bearing the Brahmana's three stolen boys and the new-born infant, restoring all four to their father.
source_excerpt: Rishikesha entered into that bundle of effulgence... Within a moment the powerful Krishna returned with the four sons of the Brāhmana and gave those three boys... and the new born baby into the hands of the Brāhmana

title: Krishna Marches on Sonitpura in Divine Form
one_line_summary: To rescue Aniruddha from Bana, Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna fly out on Garuda, Krishna assuming eight arms and innumerable heads with his weapons.
source_excerpt: Desirous of killing Vāna the lotus-eyed Keshava assumed a form having eight arms... Janārddana... assumed innumerable heads. In his four right hands he had sword, discus, club and arrows

title: Garuda Quenches Bana's Protective Fire
one_line_summary: As Bana's city-fire blazes out and robs the Yadavas of their lustre, Garuda assumes a thousand mouths, drinks the etherial Ganga and showers it down to extinguish the flames.
source_excerpt: Garuda... assumed a thousand mouths... drinking profuse water, he began to shower it on the fire... the fire was at once extinguished

title: Krishna Strikes Down Angira and the Fire-Gods
one_line_summary: Bana's fire-gods, led by the chief Angira, attack Krishna on the way, and Krishna, cutting off Angira's mace, fells him with an arrow, putting the rest to flight.
source_excerpt: cutting off his mace with crescent-shaped and sharpened arrows... Krishna... struck Angirā on the breast with a death-like-arrow. Thereat Angirā fell down bathed in blood... the four fire-gods... fled away to Vāna's city

title: Chitralekha Comes to Dwarka as Usha's Emissary
one_line_summary: Usha's friend Chitralekha travels to Dwarka to bring Aniruddha back for her mistress, and secures Narada's blessing and the Tamasika power of illusion to carry out the abduction.
source_excerpt: Chitralekha... said to the celestial saint Nārada... "I have come here as a messenger for taking Aniruddha with me"... Nārada said to her... "Accept the Tāmasa learning which can infatuate all the worlds"
notes: Backstory (flashback) of how Aniruddha came to Sonitpura.

title: Aniruddha and Usha Unite in Gandharva Marriage
one_line_summary: Chitralekha carries Aniruddha invisibly to Sonitpura, where he and Usha, who had seen each other in a dream, are united in Gandharva marriage in secret.
source_excerpt: Chitralekha... invisibly arrived where Ushā was, and she then brought and showed to Ushā the heroic Aniruddha... united in nuptials according to Gandharva rites they spent the day like a pair of Chakravākas
notes: Usha had been shown Aniruddha's portrait and pointed to him as her husband by a goddess's boon.

title: Aniruddha Routs Vana's Soldiers
one_line_summary: When Vana discovers Usha living with Aniruddha and sends his soldiers to kill him, Aniruddha seizes a Parigha and single-handedly drives the Danava host from the field.
source_excerpt: taking up a dreadful Parigha... he killed the Daityas... Having driven with Parigha the Dānavas from the battle-field the highly powerful hero Aniruddha delightfully set up a leonine shout

title: Vana Binds Aniruddha with Serpentine Shafts
one_line_summary: When Aniruddha turns Vana's own Sakti against him and wounds him, Vana resorts to Tamasika illusion and fetters Aniruddha with serpentine shafts; advised by Kumbhanda, he imprisons rather than kills him.
source_excerpt: Pradyumna's son was fettered with serpentine shafts. His body was chained with various serpents... Kumbhānda said... "He does not deserve to be slain"... handing over Aniruddha to the guards... Vāna... repaired to his own palace

title: The Goddess Durga Releases Aniruddha from His Bonds
one_line_summary: Imprisoned in Vana's city, Aniruddha hymns the goddess Katyayani, and Durga appears, cuts the serpent-nooses with her fingers, and consoles him, promising Krishna will sever Vana's thousand arms.
source_excerpt: the great goddess Durgā went where Aniruddha was kept in chains... with her fingers cut off the strong noose of serpents and then consoling Aniruddha said:—"...The holder of discus... will cut off the thousand arms of Vāna"

title: The Yadavas' Grief and Search for Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Aniruddha's wives lament and the whole Yadava assembly falls into grief; Krishna broods over the disappearance, and messengers are sent out to search mountains, forests and every country in vain.
source_excerpt: Krishna... said:—"...where has Aniruddha been exiled?... I will in battle kill him with his own people who has put on my head this foot covered with ashes"... the messengers... said:—"...we saw Aniruddha nowhere"

title: Narada Reveals Aniruddha's Captivity by Vana
one_line_summary: Narada arrives at the anxious court and tells Krishna that Vana's daughter Usha, with Chitralekha, took Aniruddha, that Vana bound him with serpent-shafts, and that he lives imprisoned awaiting rescue.
source_excerpt: Nārada... said:—"...Vāna... has a daughter by name Ushā. For her, the Apsara Chitralekhā has taken away Kāma's son... Vāna... has fettered the highly powerful Aniruddha with serpentine shafts... Aniruddha is not still deprived of life"

title: Krishna Summons Garuda and Marches to Rescue Aniruddha
one_line_summary: At Narada's bidding, Krishna summons Garuda, mounts his back with Baladeva and Pradyumna, and sets out for the distant city of Sonitpura to free Aniruddha.
source_excerpt: Govinda thought of Garuda in his mind: and he too, with folded hands, arrived before Krishna... Krishna... sat on his back. Thereupon... Halāyudha and Pradyumna... sat behind him

title: Jvara Consumes Baladeva; Krishna Saves Him
one_line_summary: The fever-demon Jvara, with three legs, three heads and six arms, hurls a burning weapon that consumes Baladeva; Krishna embraces his brother and by his touch saves him from being burnt.
source_excerpt: Jvara... hurled his consuming weapon which fell on his breast... Krishna's elder brother was however being consumed... Haladhara said to Krishna:—"...I am being consumed"... he embraced Halāyudha... He was then saved by loving Krishna from being burnt

title: Krishna Grapples with Jvara
one_line_summary: Krishna challenges Jvara and, bearing the demon's burning weapon and blows, grinds him with his arms in a fearful struggle.
source_excerpt: the powerful Krishna... experienced a burning sensation for a few moments. Immediately after the fire was put out... Jvara... struck Krishna on the neck... grinded the sky-ranging Jvara adorned with golden ornaments with his arms

title: Jvara Possesses Krishna; Krishna Expels Him
one_line_summary: The released Jvara enters Krishna's body and enfeebles him; Krishna creates a dreadful counter-Jvara from his own energy, which seizes and drags the fever out of his body.
source_excerpt: Jvara... entered into it (Krishna's body)... Krishna... created a dreadful Jvara, highly terrible unto creatures... Catching hold, by force, of the former Jvara the one, created by Krishna, presented it before him... driven out that Jvara from his body

title: Krishna Spares Jvara and Grants Him Boons
one_line_summary: Commanded by an invisible voice, Krishna spares Jvara and grants him boons — that he alone be the world's fever, divided into forms to afflict beasts, plants and mankind.
source_excerpt: an invisible voice was heard in the sky:—"...do not kill this Jvara... he is worthy of being protected by thee"... Jvara said:—"...I pray from thee for this boon only that I may be the only Jvara in this world"... dividing yourself into four parts... you are to live amongst mankind

title: Shiva and Kartikeya Enter the Battle for Vana
one_line_summary: As Vana's army flees, Shiva, eyes red with anger, ascends his lion-drawn car surrounded by his ghostly host, and Kartikeya joins him to protect Vana.
source_excerpt: Siva... had his eyes reddened with anger. And in order to protect Vāna, he stood on his lustrous car... Kumāra too ascended a car... Powerful Rudra, ascending a car drawn by lions... drove where Hari was

title: Krishna and Shiva Duel with Divine Weapons
one_line_summary: Hara and Hari exchange celestial weapons — Indra's weapon met by Shiva's fiery weapon, quenched by Krishna's Varuna weapon, then four weapons countered by four arrows — until Krishna's Vaishnava weapon routs the ghostly host.
source_excerpt: Vishnu discharged Indra's weapon at Rudra... Hara discharged the highly dreadful fiery weapon... Vāsudeva took up Vāruna weapon... the fire of the fiery weapon was extinguished... Mādhava discharged his Vaishnava weapon... all the Bhutas, Yakshas and Asuras... fled on all sides

title: Kartikeya Duels the Yadavas; Krishna Counters Brahmashira
one_line_summary: Kartikeya rides out and strikes Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna; when he discharges the world-destroying Brahmashira weapon, Krishna's discus blots out its lustre, and he strikes down Kartikeya's burning Sakti.
source_excerpt: Guha (Kārtikeya) drove towards Krishna, Baladeva and Pradyumna and struck them with hundreds of dreadful and sharpened arrows... Keshava took up his discus the destroyer and counteractor of all weapons... that discus... clouded, with its lustre, that of Brahmashira weapon

title: Kottavi Intervenes to Save Kartikeya
one_line_summary: As Krishna raises his discus against Kartikeya, the naked goddess Kottavi, sent by Mahadeva, intervenes, and Krishna, unable to strike before her, puts away his discus.
source_excerpt: the beautiful Kottavi, at the mandate of Mahādeva, came there naked for protecting Kumāra... Seeing the goddess stand before Kumāra the large-armed Krishna was baffled... put away his discus

title: Vana Vaunts and Fights Krishna
one_line_summary: Vana boasts of his thousand arms, but Krishna answers and, with the Sarnga bow, sunders Vana's car, horses and standard, then strips him of crown, mail, bow and shield until he swoons.
source_excerpt: Vāna... said... "how you will be able to fight with me who have a thousand arms?"... Keshava sundered Vāna's car, with horses and standards, into pieces... separated from Vāna's person his highly lustrous crown, coat of mail, bow and shield... Vāna lost his consciousness

title: Kottavi Again Intercedes; Krishna Vows to Cut Vana's Arms
one_line_summary: When the naked goddess Kottavi again stands between them to honour her boon of protection to Vana, Krishna vows to cut off Vana's thousand arms, leaving only two, while sparing his life.
source_excerpt: Lamvā... appeared naked before Vasudeva... said:—"...I conferred on him a boon saying that I would protect him"... Krishna... said:—"...I will forsooth cut off to-day his thousand arms... Your son will live even if Vāna has two arms"

title: Krishna Cuts Off Vana's Thousand Arms
one_line_summary: Krishna discharges the thousand-bladed Sudarshana discus, which moves invisibly through the battle and chops off Vana's thousand arms, leaving him with only two.
source_excerpt: taking up that wonderful discus... discharged it and cut off Vāna's arms... Gradually cutting off Vāna's thousand arms and making him the owner of only two the Sudarshana discus returned into Krishna's hands

title: Shiva Intercedes for Vana; Vana Dances and Wins Boons
one_line_summary: Shiva intercedes for Vana's life, Krishna withdraws his discus, and the armless Vana, bidden by Nandi, dances before Shiva and receives boons, becoming the Pramatha chief Mahakala.
source_excerpt: Mahadeva said:—"...I have promised Vāna protection... desist"... Krishna... "I withdraw my discus. At thy request Vāna will live"... Vāna... began to dance... Mahādeva... said:—"I am pleased with you... pray for a boon"
notes: Vana becomes Mahakala, first of the Pramathas, and receives several boons from Shiva.

title: Krishna Finds and Frees Aniruddha
one_line_summary: Krishna and the Yadavas enter Vana's inner apartments, and at the mere sight of Garuda the serpents binding Aniruddha fall away as arrows, freeing him.
source_excerpt: Baladeva, Krishna, Pradyumna, Narada and Suparna entered into the female appartment for releasing Aniruddha. Seeing Garuda, all the huge serpents, which stuck to Aniruddha's person in the shape of arrows, at once left him

title: Krishna Celebrates Aniruddha's Wedding and Grants the Kingdom to Kumbhanda
one_line_summary: Krishna celebrates Aniruddha and Usha's wedding, and confers Vana's kingdom on the minister Kumbhanda, who had counselled mercy toward Aniruddha.
source_excerpt: Krishna... said:—"...You will now become the king of this kingdom. I confer this kingdom on you"... Janārddana celebrated the wedding festival of Aniruddha

title: Krishna Fights Varuna for the Celestial Cows
one_line_summary: Seeking Vana's celestial kine in Varuna's charge for Satyabhama, Krishna routs Varuna's army and battles Varuna, whose Varuna-weapon is consumed by Krishna's Vaishnava weapon.
source_excerpt: the kine of Vāna... drinking whose milk a man becomes immortal... Varuna's... army... were all routed by the high-souled Keshava... with the energy of Vaishnava weapon that water was ablaze
notes: Satyabhama had asked Krishna for the kine, whose milk wards off decrepitude and fever.

title: Varuna Pleads His Promise; Krishna Relents
one_line_summary: Varuna pleads his vow to Vana never to part with the cows, and Krishna, honouring his truthfulness, releases both Varuna and the cows and returns to Dwarka amid the rejoicing citizens.
source_excerpt: Varuna said... "I had formerly promised, that if alive I would never give away these kine"... Krishna... said:—"...you are truthful and therefore for pleasing you I let loose Vāna's cows. And you too are released"

title: Usha Is Welcomed into the Yadu Family
one_line_summary: Back in Dwarka, Ahuka bids a festival; Usha is conducted to Aniruddha's house amid benedictions, and Devaki, Revati and Rukmini welcome her with tears of joy, closing the Vana episode.
source_excerpt: Ahuka said... "Do thou undertake a great festival for Aniruddha's return and wedding"... Devaki, Revati and... Rukshmini shed tears of joy... Ushā... lived in their palace and enjoyed best of happiness
notes: Chapter 277 closes the Vishnu Parva (Part 1); the Bhavishya Parva follows.
